speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; to help me understand your condition, how long have you had this wound and what does it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-thrombotic syndrome (chronic venous insufficiency).

Given the history of a DVT five years ago, long-standing bilateral leg swelling, and family history, your current non-healing wound is likely a venous stasis ulcer. Have you noticed any redness, warmth, or drainage from the wound, and how is it changing in size?
